text:
maria: Quick heads-up — Large enterprise buyer (FinRegCo) sent a CAIQ. They flagged KMS ownership and rotation, and asked whether we can support customer-managed keys for hosted API during the POC. Deadline: Thu EOD. Need final wording for CAIQ responses + POC deliverables.

sam: @maria thanks. Can you paste the specific CAIQ questions? which CX team is leading? :eyes:

maria: Pasted snippet from vendor portal — Qs are around encryption key mgmt and logging. Example: "Does your service support customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption of customer data at rest?" and "Who is responsible for KMS rotation?"

elaine: Short answer we already gave in other deals: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys; Dedicated/Private = customer-managed KMS via KMS/HSM integration. We should make the CAIQ answer explicit that for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and keys are managed by Redwood under our infra (SOC2 controls), while Private supports customer KMS.

owen: Agree. Also add note about key rotation: For Hosted we rotate per our ops policy (do not promise exact cadence here). For Private/Dedicated customer can rotate per their KMS policies. Avoid stating exact rotation period unless security approves.

julie: Legal: don't promise rotation cadence in CAIQ — say "rotation is performed by Redwood in accordance with our security policy" for Hosted. For customer-managed keys say "customer controls rotation". That keeps scope narrow.

sam: I'll draft CAIQ answers. Proposed text:

```text
Q: Do you support CMKs for data at rest?
A: Hosted API: No (Redwood-managed keys). Dedicated & Private: Yes — customers can configure KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM) when deploying Private or Dedicated with VPC. See our POC note below.

Q: Who is responsible for key rotation?
A: Hosted: Redwood performs rotation in accordance with our security policy. Dedicated/Private: Customer-managed; customer controls rotation schedule.
```

maria: That looks good. Add pointer to SOC2 + audit logs for Hosted keys and mention that we provide exportable audit logs in Dedicated/Private.

elaine: Also include short POC checklist so procurement knows what's required:
- POC env: Private (preferred) or Dedicated if they need predictable latency
- KMS: If they require CMK during POC, we need their KMS IAM role + network peering (for Private)
- Data: sample dataset (anonymized)
- Timeline: 2 weeks setup, 2 weeks run
- Pricing ask: 30% off for first 3 months on Dedicated capacity

maria: buyer pushed back on 30% — wants pricing baked into CAIQ comments. Keep pricing out of CAIQ; handle separately in procurement email.

sam: Agreed. I'll omit pricing from CAIQ reply. I'll add the POC checklist as an attachment in the vendor portal.

owen: @sam one thing — ensure CAIQ answer references control IDs so their risk team can map answers (e.g., CCM-EN-02, CCM-LOG-01). That helps reviewers.

sam: noted. I'll tag those control IDs in the response and cc security.

deploy-bot: Document uploaded to vendor portal: https://vendor-portal.example.com/submission/FR-POC-998

maria: Perfect. Can someone review final text before EOD Thursday? @owen @elaine @julie

owen: I'll review by 15:00 today.

elaine: Same, can sign off if wording follows what's above.

julie: I'll quick-scan legal phrasing, should be fine.

maria: Thanks team :pray: — I'll ping procurement+buyer after submission.
